question: What is the primary structural abnormality in red blood cells of individuals with sickle cell anaemia?

options.B: Polymerization of abnormal haemoglobin S leading to a crescent shape
options.C: Enlarged biconcave discs with increased deformability
options.D: Complete absence of any haemoglobin molecules

explanation: Deoxygenated haemoglobin S polymerizes to form rigid structures that distort red blood cells into a stiff, crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why do patients with sickle cell anaemia develop chronic haemolytic anaemia?

options.A: Sickled cells have a drastically shortened lifespan of 10 to 20 days
options.B: The bone marrow completely stops producing red blood cells
options.C: Platelets destroy all circulating white blood cells
options.D: Excess oxygen causes red blood cells to rupture immediately

explanation: Sickle cells live only 10 to 20 days compared to normal cells, leading to rapid destruction and chronic haemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What is the inheritance pattern of sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, requiring two abnormal genes for the disease to manifest. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: If both parents are carriers of the sickle cell trait (HbAS), what is the probability of having a child with sickle cell anaemia (HbSS) in each pregnancy?
explanation: When both parents carry the trait, there is a 25 percent chance per pregnancy of a child inheriting two abnormal genes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is dactylitis, often seen as an early sign in infants with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Sudden swelling and pain in the hands and feet due to bone microinfarctions
options.B: Infection of the middle ear caused by trapped bacteria
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the skin resulting from liver failure
options.D: Paralysis of the lower extremities due to spinal cord compression

explanation: Dactylitis, or hand-foot syndrome, causes painful swelling in the hands and feet due to vaso-occlusion in small bones. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why do patients with sickle cell anaemia have an increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacterial infections?

options.A: They produce excessive amounts of white blood cells
options.B: Functional asplenia develops early due to repeated splenic infarctions
options.C: Their skin barriers are weakened by chronic dehydration
options.D: Haemoglobin S directly attracts pathogenic bacteria

explanation: Repeated infarctions damage the spleen, leading to functional asplenia and impairing the body's ability to fight encapsulated bacteria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which type of crisis involves the sudden pooling of blood in the spleen, leading to hypovolemic shock?
explanation: Splenic sequestration crisis occurs when blood rapidly pools in the spleen, causing severe hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: What viral infection is frequently associated with triggering an aplastic crisis in sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Parvovirus B19 infects red blood cell precursors, temporarily halting erythropoiesis and precipitating an aplastic crisis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the definitive diagnostic test used to identify sickle cell anaemia and determine haemoglobin variants?
explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis separates haemoglobin types by electrical charge, definitively identifying abnormal variants like HbS. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: What do Howell-Jolly bodies observed on a peripheral blood smear indicate in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Howell-Jolly bodies are remnants of nuclear DNA normally removed by a functioning spleen; their presence indicates hyposplenism. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: What prophylactic medication is routinely administered to infants diagnosed with sickle cell anaemia to prevent severe infections?
explanation: Daily oral penicillin prophylaxis is given to infants to prevent life-threatening pneumococcal infections due to functional asplenia. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why is folic acid supplementation commonly prescribed for patients with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: To cure the genetic mutation permanently
options.B: To support increased erythropoiesis caused by chronic haemolysis
options.C: To prevent dehydration during hot weather
options.D: To eliminate the risk of vaso-occlusive crises

explanation: Folic acid supports rapid red blood cell production in the bone marrow to compensate for chronic haemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which of the following lifestyle instructions is crucial for a nurse to emphasize to a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.B: Maintaining adequate daily hydration to prevent red blood cell sickling
options.C: Engaging in exhaustive exercise to boost immunity
options.D: Avoiding all vaccinations to prevent immune overload

explanation: Adequate hydration reduces blood viscosity and helps prevent red blood cells from sickling and causing vaso-occlusion. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: When managing pain during a vaso-occlusive crisis, what attitude should the nurse adopt?

options.A: Assume the patient is exaggerating pain to obtain medication
options.B: Withhold analgesics until laboratory results confirm the pain level
options.C: Acknowledge the patient's pain experience and administer prescribed analgesics promptly
options.D: Rely solely on non-pharmacological methods like warm baths

explanation: Nurses must take patient reports of pain seriously and administer analgesics promptly without prejudice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which long-term complication involves the death of bone tissue due to interrupted blood supply, commonly affecting the femoral head?
explanation: Avascular necrosis occurs when vaso-occlusion cuts off blood supply to bone tissue, leading to tissue death, frequently in the femoral head. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse within a multi-disciplinary sickle cell follow-up team?

options.B: Coordinating care, monitoring medication adherence, and advocating for the patient

explanation: Nurses coordinate multi-disciplinary care, track compliance with therapies like hydroxyurea, and advocate for comprehensive patient needs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)
